label: C / FACE Case 5

paper-64gib.label: 64 GiB paper configuration
paper-64gib.note: FACE Case 5 provides 64 GiB of local HBM per NPU in the paper configuration.

validation-160gib.label: 160 GiB validation extension
validation-160gib.note: Validation-only capacity extension for workloads that require 160 GiB of local HBM per NPU.

validation-die-64g.label: 64 GB die-derived validation capacity
validation-die-64g.note: Die-backend aligned capacity: exactly the HBM capacity derived by the die cost library from the die node (4 x 16 GB), required by config_resolver when the die node is present.

validation-coarse-144g.label: 144 GB coarse_die_v2 die-derived capacity
validation-coarse-144g.note: coarse_die_v2 backend aligned: exactly 2 rows x 2 stacks x 36 GB per die

notes: The physical mesh is row-major with 9 rows and 6 columns.
The analytical network lists dimensions as columns then rows.

The die node (stage C, 2026-10-03) replaces compute.peak-perf-tflops: peak compute, local-mem bandwidth and capacity are derived by the shared die cost library (mutually exclusive with a compute node).
D2D latency is modeled as a per-hop adjacent-link latency and is independent of the on-die noc-width-bits.
Remote-memory expansion is disabled for this repository configuration.
The capacity profile describes local HBM placement per NPU.

User-authorized engineering comparison point (2026-10-16): 10 x 10 Core grid on a 25 mm x 32 mm compute Die (800 mm2), 0.75 MiB SRAM/Core and 512-bit NoC. Architectural PE peak is 126.6 INT4 TOPS, numerically compared with the TX8 128 BF16 TFLOPS reference; precision and independent measurement are not equivalent. Vec FP32-equivalent peak is 12.65728 T eq-op/s, not the TX8 1 T reference. Legacy HBM remains the preserved 4 x 16 GB / 410 GB/s per-stack reference (64 GB and 1640 GB/s), not current DOCX HBM3E.

coarse_die_v2 factory default (stage 2, 2026-10-18): the checked-in node is coarse-die carrying the complete coarse_die_v2 descriptor (source revision 41f119135fd2d4cc87292f59b4b00adc918eece0); peak compute, local-mem bandwidth and capacity derive through libcoarse_die_cabi.so and the resolver materializes resolved_die_model.json (mutually exclusive with the die and compute nodes; the mesh_die_v1 die-node form stays supported by config_resolver for fixtures). validation-coarse-144g mirrors the coarse-derived 144 GB (2 rows x 2 stacks x 36 GB per die); the legacy paper-64gib/validation-160gib/validation-die-64g entries remain for other uses but fail the coarse capacity alignment.
